contentBlocks.text: This week you built a real toolkit for understanding any community in the world — your own or one far away. Let's review it all.

Quick review: every community has people, environment, and traditions (Day 1). Culture includes language, food, clothing, art, and celebrations (Day 2). Punjab is a real South Asian region named for its five rivers, divided between India and Pakistan, and known as a farming 'breadbasket' (Day 3). You compared your own community to a Punjab farming community, finding real similarities and differences without ranking either as better (Day 4). Use this same three-part framework (people, environment, traditions) the next time you learn about any new place — it works for any community anywhere.
Great work this week — you now have a real framework for understanding communities and cultures anywhere in the world, and real knowledge of one specific place: Punjab.

objectives: Recall the people/environment/traditions community framework and the culture vocabulary from the week
Recall real geographic facts about Punjab
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Complete the cumulative review worksheet, mixing all 4 days' concepts.
3. Discuss any mismatches or uncertain answers together before finishing.
4. Celebrate finishing the first full week of this unit — remind the child this same framework will return in future world-communities units.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to use their Day 1-4 worksheets as a reference during review rather than working from memory alone
Ready for more: ask them to apply the framework to a third community (real or hypothetical) not covered this week
This is a good checkpoint to note which day's concept needs the most re-teaching before moving to next week's unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. People, environment, and traditions. 2. Language, food, clothing, art/music, and celebrations. 3. 'Land of five rivers.' 4. A place that grows far more food than its own people need — a 'breadbasket.'
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates the week's C3 Framework Geography and Culture content before the unit moves to a new topic, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established in every other unit this session.
